contributions.statement: Accept agent-written code on a fresh random sample of cases drawn after the candidate is committed (hashed), never on cases the agent saw; at 500 cases and 5% tolerance a zero-failure audit needs 54 cases versus 475 known tests.
contributions.evidence: §4 Theorems 4.10-4.15, Table 2 exact audit sizes; applied post hoc to 600 recorded candidates (83-case audit -> 0.074 expected false acceptances); the audit never gated live development (audit).

contributions.statement: Before building an LLM adversarial tester, compare it against property-based tests drawn from a production-like input generator (e.g. jqwik for Java); here they were statistically indistinguishable, and one-shot LLM-written tests were no better than the public example alone.
contributions.evidence: Table 6: Dynamic informed - Static property -0.024 (CI -0.097 to +0.043); Static LLM - Public only +0.064 n.s.; 30 blocks, one toy task, gpt-4.1-mini, no-tool coder.

reason: The audit-sizing result gives a concrete, checkable acceptance rule that separates development feedback from acceptance; the empirical part is a single toy task and only supports a hypothesis.
